original_test_intent: Read the vendor-defined BIOS SD/SystemDefaults representation, if documented as a resource, and validate a privacy-controlled defaults snapshot without applying defaults or changing BIOS state.
original_method: Resolve the intended System BIOS links, use firmware/vendor metadata to establish SD's read-only GET contract, retrieve it once with trusted access, validate resource/default schema, and export approved redacted fields.
manual_activity: Supply firmware/vendor documentation proving the SD endpoint and GET semantics, intended target, defaults schema/field scope, secure credentials/TLS and evidence policy, then authorize the read.
required_inputs: Advertised BIOS/SD link or vendor method contract
Approved defaults field allowlist and redaction
safety_requirements: Do not infer SD meaning from its name
Do not GET an action target unless documented safe
Use GET only after method proof
agent_execution_scope: Capture HTTP metadata and restricted raw hash
Validate resource identity/default schema and allowlisted fields
Export redacted snapshot and no-mutation proof
engineer_actions: Approve vendor SD semantics, field scope and privacy policy

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Discover and validate the vendor resource contract before any request, then use a schema-aware allowlist read.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds semantic method proof, correct dependencies, trusted access and BIOS-default privacy controls.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Covers read-only defaults representation only and explicitly excludes applying defaults.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: If SD is not a resource or GET has side effects on this firmware, the case cannot proceed under this method.

project_override_considerations: An OEM Redfish extension or supported SDK is acceptable only with pinned vendor documentation that identifies method, response schema and side effects. Standard BIOS GET cannot substitute for SD-specific defaults coverage.
expected_evidence: Immutable target/firmware and vendor SD contract
Advertised BIOS→SD link and allowed GET proof
HTTP metadata and restricted raw hash
Redacted defaults snapshot with typed fields
Proof no action/default application/BIOS/reboot/log mutation occurred

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item, path and procedure consistently request GET; ambiguity comes from undocumented vendor SD semantics, not competing Master instructions.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The vendor contract and schema are identifiable prerequisites. If supplied documentation cannot prove read-only semantics, execution reaches the recorded blocked condition.

review_improvement: Prevents a vendor-specific name from being treated as proof of safety and confines the case to a documented, privacy-controlled defaults read.
independent_technical_reasoning: `SD` is not self-describing: on one firmware it may expose SystemDefaults data, while on another it may be absent or adjacent to a reset action. HTTP GET is normally read-only but must not be sent blindly to an OEM action-like target. The resource must be advertised or vendor-documented, and its fields need a BIOS security allowlist because default values can reveal boot and protection policy even without mutation.
